title: still present since round 3: entering demo clobbers a live landlord session — auth AND the real CSRF token are overwritten; exit downgrades auth to NotAsked with no restore
evidence:
client.gleam enter_demo: '          auth: Success(landlord),
          csrf_token: "demo-csrf-token",' (unconditional, no preservation of the prior values); model.gleam clear_demo_state: '    demo_mode: False,
    demo_store: None,
    auth: NotAsked,' — and clear_demo_state's field list contains no csrf_token restore.
detail: A logged-in landlord who opens /demo loses SPA auth state and their real CSRF token is replaced by the literal 'demo-csrf-token'. On exit the session cookie is intact but the SPA must re-auth, and any state-changing request fired before re-auth carries the fake token.
recommended_fix: Preserve pre-demo auth and csrf_token on entry and restore both on clear_demo_state (or document the swap and re-check session on exit).

title: still present since round 3: latent policy re-acceptance modal can surface in demo and UserAcceptedPolicy fires a real accept_policy POST — demo_update does not intercept it
location: client/src/client.gleam:1356-1367 (UserAcceptedPolicy arm); client/src/demo/demo_update.gleam (no UserAcceptedPolicy arm — grep returns nothing); client/src/demo/demo_fixtures.gleam:26 (accepted_policy_version pinned)
evidence:
client.gleam: '    UserAcceptedPolicy ->
      case model.policy_reaccept_loading {
        True -> #(model, effect.none())
        False -> #(
          Model(..model, policy_reaccept_loading: True),
          auth_api.accept_policy(' — and 'grep -n UserAcceptedPolicy client/src/demo/demo_update.gleam' yields no handle arm (only the msg import list in client.gleam).
detail: Latent: the fixture pins accepted_policy_version 2026-05-23 (conformance-test held), but a server policy bump while server_policy_version is populated surfaces the modal inside demo and the accept click fires a real POST with the fake demo CSRF token.
recommended_fix: Intercept UserAcceptedPolicy in demo_update (no-op with toast) and keep the lint manifest honest.

title: still present since round 3: Declan fixture household income (EUR 6,500/mo) is 1.86x his stated primary income (EUR 3,500/mo) with co_applicant_count 0 and one occupant
evidence: '\"employment_status\":\"self_employed\",\"employer_name\":null,\"job_title\":\"Plumber (self-employed)\",\"employment_duration\":\"6 years\",\"monthly_income_cents\":350000' ... '\"num_occupants\":1' ... '\"household_monthly_income_cents\":650000,\"co_applicant_count\":0}' — all on the single app_declan_json line 87.
detail: Household exceeds primary by EUR 3,000/mo with no co-applicant and no income source in the story (the guarantor's 310k does not match the gap). The demo detail page shows a household income nobody in the story earns.
recommended_fix: Set household_monthly_income_cents to 350000 for the single-occupant story, or add a second income source to the fixture narrative.

title: still present since round 3: report_download_test pins the analysis-id mapping but not baked-asset presence — a deleted or misnamed PDF 404s silently in the demo
detail: The only permitted demo network touch (the static report fetch) is unpinned at the asset level: id mapping is proven, but nothing asserts the eight report-*.pdf files exist on disk, so a missing asset 404s at download time.
recommended_fix: Add a build-time check asserting every report_filenames entry has a matching file under server/priv/static/demo/.

title: still present since round 3: pdf_prebake regen docs promise a positional CLI arg that main() never reads — the env var is the real switch
detail: Following the documented regen command silently bakes into the default priv dir instead of the passed path; the operator believes they targeted a directory they did not.
recommended_fix: Fix the header to document RT_DEMO_PRIV_DIR (or read the positional arg).
